headline: ASX closes up 0.38% as oil slumps nearly 4%, Trump rattles sabres at Iran at the UN, and OpenAI drops GPT-6 while Anthropic fires back with Claude Opus 5.5.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS bounced +1.21% today, likely catching a bid alongside broader lithium market sentiment — forecasts out this week point to strong long-term demand for lithium battery storage, with grid-scale storage expected to drive 18-22% compound annual growth through to 2035. The underlying lithium price story remains challenged, but today's session was a small positive for a beaten-up stock.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI edged up 0.53% today, tracking positive sentiment around AI stocks on the ASX. The backdrop is busy — OpenAI launched GPT-6 Sol and Luna, Anthropic dropped Claude Opus 5.5, and the AI sector is in a price-war phase with cheaper models rolling out fast. Good for AI adoption broadly, which underpins this ETF's long-term thesis.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS ticked up 0.3% at today's ASX close, reflecting modest overnight strength in US equities last session. This ETF tracks the entire US share market, so it moves with the broad US mood — which remains cautiously positive heading into the Northern Hemisphere autumn earnings season.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.13% — a quiet session for this diversified fund, which holds a mix of Aussie and international shares. No specific catalyst today; it just drifted slightly higher with the broader ASX.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped a fractional 0.13% today. Emerging markets are feeling some pressure from the stronger US dollar and ongoing Middle East tension weighing on global risk appetite. Nothing alarming for a long-term holder — this is normal day-to-day noise.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: No live price data available for GOOG today — US markets haven't opened yet. Last night's close was $350.87 USD. Google is in the middle of a competitive AI arms race, with OpenAI's GPT-6 and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 both launching this week, keeping pressure on Alphabet's Gemini.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: No live price data for MSFT yet — US markets open tonight. Last session MSFT rose about 1.59% as investors look ahead to Q1 revenue results. Microsoft's Azure and Copilot AI suite continue to be the key growth story that the market is pricing in.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO's US price isn't available yet — markets open tonight. Last close was $209.92 USD. News this week: Take-Two's CEO commented that a PC release date for GTA 6 is still unconfirmed, though he expressed optimism it's 'becoming' a reality. GTA 6 remains the big catalyst the market is waiting on for this stock.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Hold through the volatility
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals popped +1.21% today but is still down nearly 38% on your total investment. The lithium market remains oversupplied and uncertain, but new forecasts point to strong long-term demand from grid storage. The long-term thesis is intact — hold and be patient. Don't let a bad run spook you into selling near the bottom.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — Hold, AI sector is buzzing
watch_today.detail: Up 0.53% today, but still down 8.77% overall. This week has been huge for AI — GPT-6, Claude Opus 5.5, UK parliament hearings, and an antitrust suit against the big players all in 48 hours. The long-term case for AI adoption driving this ETF is strong. Short-term dips are noise. Hold.

watch_today.title: RBA rate rise looking more likely — watch your mortgage and bonds exposure
watch_today.detail: The RBA governor has explicitly said the job market is running too 'hot' and rates may need to rise. CBA and ANZ both shifted their rate forecasts this week to price in a hike. This is bad news for borrowers and for rate-sensitive assets, but your VDHG holds a chunk of bonds — rising rates can weigh on bond prices in the short term. Long-term holders: sit tight, this is priced into diversified funds over time.

watch_today.title: VTS.AX — Hold, US market steady
watch_today.detail: VTS is your best performer — up 4.2% overall and ticking higher. It tracks the whole US market, which is broadly holding up well. Tonight's US open will be worth watching given Middle East tension and oil's sharp drop. No reason to change anything here for a long-term holder.

watch_today.title: Oil crashes nearly 4% — watch inflation and energy stocks
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) dropped $3.66 to $90.93 — a 3.87% fall in a single session. Lower oil usually means lower petrol prices for everyday Aussies over the coming weeks, and it takes some pressure off inflation. It's also a sign that markets may be pricing in some kind of Iran deal after Trump's UN speech, which could ease Middle East supply fears.

watch_today.title: TTWO — Hold ahead of GTA 6 news
watch_today.detail: Take-Two's CEO dropped a hint this week that a GTA 6 PC release is 'becoming' a reality, but no date confirmed. The console launch remains the near-term catalyst. Your cost basis is $651 AUD invested — hold and wait for GTA 6 to drive revenue. This is a multi-year story.

world.summary: Trump rattled the UN with Iran war threats while dangling a deal, oil prices tumbled sharply, global economic forecasters are cautiously optimistic despite Middle East risks, and former Canadian PM Trudeau is reinventing himself as a public intellectual.

stories.title: Trump Tells UN He Could 'Annihilate' Iran — But Expects a Deal After Midterms
stories.why_it_matters: At the UN General Assembly, Trump delivered a stark warning to Iran — saying the US has the ability to 'annihilate' the country — while simultaneously hinting he expects to cut a deal after the US midterm elections. The Iranian president also arrived in New York this week, suggesting back-channel talks may be live. This combination of threats and diplomacy is why oil markets are jittery: a deal could flood markets with Iranian oil, pushing prices down further.

stories.title: Iran Flights Canceled as New US Aviation Sanctions Bite
stories.why_it_matters: New US aviation sanctions on Iran took effect this week, grounding Iranian flights. This is part of a broader squeeze on Tehran that's running in parallel with Trump's UN diplomacy. For everyday Australians it's mostly background noise, but it adds to global uncertainty — especially for energy prices and Middle East stability — which flows through to petrol prices and your investments in international shares.

stories.title: OECD: Global Economy More Resilient Than Expected, But Middle East is the Big Risk
stories.why_it_matters: The OECD released its latest global growth outlook and said the world economy is holding up better than feared, despite the ongoing Middle East conflict. The World Economic Forum echoed this but flagged the Middle East as the single biggest threat to the outlook. For investors, this is broadly reassuring — the global economy isn't rolling over — but it's a reminder that an escalation in the Middle East could change the picture fast.

stories.title: Trudeau Reinvents Himself at Brown University — Discusses US-Canada Relations and Global Conflict
stories.why_it_matters: Former Canadian PM Justin Trudeau, who stepped down earlier this year, is now lecturing at Brown University in the US. He spoke on the state of US-Canada relations (strained under Trump), global conflict, and the power of storytelling in politics. It's an unusual sight — a recent world leader taking a step back to reflect publicly — and signals how much the political landscape has shifted in North America under Trump's second term.

stories.title: Houthi-Saudi Conflict: What It Means for the US (and the World)
stories.why_it_matters: The Council on Foreign Relations published a major explainer on the Houthi-Saudi conflict and what it means for the United States. The Houthis (backed by Iran) have been attacking Red Sea shipping lanes, disrupting global trade and pushing up freight costs. For Australians, this matters because disrupted shipping routes can affect the cost of goods and add to inflation pressures — and it's one more thread in the complex Middle East knot that's keeping oil markets on edge.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 closed up 0.38% to 8,765 — a solid session. Oil was the big mover globally, crashing nearly 4% on hopes of an Iran deal. The Aussie dollar slipped. US markets open tonight — last session the S&P 500 sat at 7,765 and the NASDAQ at 27,122.

politics.summary: The RBA is now openly flagging an interest rate rise to cool the jobs market, and Australia's social media algorithm opt-out laws have sparked a rare and heated diplomatic clash with the United States.

stories.title: RBA Governor Signals Rate Rise Coming — Jobs Market Too Hot
stories.why_it_matters: RBA Governor Michele Bullock has said explicitly that 'heat' needs to come out of the labour market, and that interest rates may need to rise further to cool inflation. Both CBA and ANZ have now shifted their forecasts to price in a rate hike — meaning Australia's big banks expect your mortgage repayments to go up again. AFR reports the RBA is willing to drive up unemployment to get inflation under control, which is a tough but deliberate trade-off.

stories.title: US Attacks Australia's Social Media Algorithm Opt-Out Law as 'Censorship'
stories.why_it_matters: Australia is pushing laws that would allow social media users to opt out of algorithmic content feeds (meaning platforms like TikTok and Instagram couldn't use personalised recommendations without consent). The US government has formally criticised this as 'censorship', calling it a threat to free speech. PM Albanese is defending the laws, while critics including the US are saying it's government overreach into how tech companies run their platforms. This is a rare and significant diplomatic spat between two close allies.

stories.title: Former Treasurer Says Only a 'Financial Crisis' Will Force Real Economic Reform
stories.why_it_matters: A former Australian treasurer made the blunt observation this week that structural economic reform in Australia — things like tax reform, housing supply fixes, and productivity improvements — is effectively impossible in the current political environment and will only happen if there's a genuine financial crisis forcing politicians' hands. It's a pessimistic but widely-held view in economics circles, and it speaks to why big reform feels so hard to achieve in Canberra.

stories.title: Albanese Defends Social Media Laws as Trump Pushes Back
stories.why_it_matters: PM Albanese is standing firm on Australia's proposed algorithm opt-out laws despite pushback from both the Trump administration and US tech companies, who are labelling the laws as censorship. Australian Greens and some Labor backbenchers are urging Albanese to rebuff what they see as foreign interference in domestic policy. The outcome matters for companies like Meta and Google that operate in Australia — and by extension, for your GOOG holding.

ai.summary: A massive week for AI: OpenAI launched GPT-6 (with two variants), Anthropic fired back with Claude Opus 5.5, both companies are cutting prices, and UK Parliament has summoned the big AI companies to explain themselves. Meanwhile, Trump told the UN he's against AI regulation.

stories.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna — A Two-Model Approach
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has released GPT-6 in two flavours: Sol (optimised for speed and everyday tasks) and Luna (a deeper reasoning model for complex problems). This is significant because it's the first time OpenAI has launched a split model family under a single generation — essentially offering different brains for different jobs. Benchmarks show GPT-6 Sol and Luna competitive with or ahead of rivals including Claude Opus 5.5 and Google's Gemini. This keeps pressure on Alphabet's AI business.

stories.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Opus 5.5 — Cheaper and More Capable
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 within hours of OpenAI's GPT-6 launch — a clear shot across the bow. Claude Opus 5.5 is positioned as cheaper than its predecessor while delivering improved performance, particularly on complex reasoning tasks. This is part of a broader price war in AI: both Anthropic and OpenAI are slashing costs to win enterprise customers. Cheaper AI is good for businesses adopting it, and good for ETFs like GXAI that hold companies building on these models.

stories.title: UK Parliament Summons Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic to AI Safety Hearing
stories.why_it_matters: The UK Parliament's Business Committee has formally invited the chiefs of Meta, Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic to appear before MPs to answer questions about AI safety. This is happening as AI capabilities are advancing faster than regulation. The hearing signals growing political seriousness in the UK about who is accountable when AI causes harm — and it comes as a separate antitrust lawsuit has been filed in the US against Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX. Regulatory pressure is building on all sides.

stories.title: Trump Rejects AI Regulation at the UN — Compares It to Climate Policy
stories.why_it_matters: In his UN address, Trump said he opposes AI regulation, drawing a parallel to his rejection of climate science — framing both as areas where he believes government interference does more harm than good. This matters because the US is the world's biggest AI market, and without US regulatory leadership, global rules will be fragmented. For investors in AI stocks, less regulation in the near term could mean faster growth — but also higher long-term risk if safety incidents occur.

stories.title: Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX Hit with Antitrust Lawsuit in the US
stories.why_it_matters: A new antitrust lawsuit has been filed in US federal court (Northern District of California) targeting Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, and SpaceX, alleging anti-competitive behaviour in the AI space. This is early days — antitrust cases take years — but it's a meaningful signal that regulators and litigants are starting to treat the AI industry the way they once treated Big Tech search and social media. For GOOG holders, this adds to existing antitrust pressure on Alphabet.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 3 is here with Dolphins v Roosters on Friday night at Suncorp — right in your backyard. The AFL Grand Final is days away with a Fremantle angle getting Maccas excited, and the Roos coaching job search is getting messier.

stories.title: Dolphins Back Hit With Ban Ahead of Roosters Finals Clash
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins have been dealt a blow ahead of Friday night's Finals Week 3 clash against the Roosters at Suncorp Stadium — a key back has been suspended. Meanwhile Fox Sports reports the words spoken in the Roosters' dressing room after last week's miracle win are still ringing around the club. Kick-off is 7:50 PM Friday — right in your backyard on the Gold Coast. Big game with a finals berth on the line.

stories.title: NRL's Next Superstar: The Rise Shaped by Wayne Bennett
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports ran a deep feature on the NRL's latest rising star — a player whose career was transformed by a Wayne Bennett conversation that changed his approach to the game. Bennett's influence continues to loom large in the competition even as he steps back from day-to-day coaching. Worth a read if you love the game's human stories.

stories.title: AFL Grand Final Preview: Everything You Need to Know
stories.why_it_matters: The 2026 AFL Grand Final is just around the corner and News.com.au has published a full guide. Maccas is offering free Big Macs to West Australians if Fremantle win — a sign the Dockers are genuine contenders in this year's decider. The AFL Trade Period also kicks off right after the grand final, with AFL Trade Radio returning to cover what's shaping up as a bumper off-season.

stories.title: Another Premiership Coach Pulls Out of North Melbourne's Head Coach Search
stories.why_it_matters: Another experienced premiership-winning coach has taken their name out of contention for the North Melbourne head coaching role. The Roos' search for a new senior coach is becoming increasingly difficult, with multiple high-profile candidates stepping away. It's a challenging rebuild at Arden Street, and the coaching vacuum makes the club's path back to finals even harder.
